findings.title: Failed cycles with mixed reasons fall through to the skip-only label
findings.trigger: Both queues are active; the missing queue contains only malformed records, and the cutoff queue's configured tag cannot be resolved. No search is accepted.
findings.execution_path: Tag resolution marks cutoff unevaluated; malformed filtering records a missing-queue skip; CycleTally.to_record grades the cycle failed; cycle_view produces two rows; the template rejects the details branch because the grade is failed, then accepts the skipped-record branch despite ns.unevaluated being positive.
findings.consequence: The collapsed red card says 'Show 1 skipped record' although its two rows include an unevaluated queue. It omits that problem from the summary and bypasses the intended failure wording for the Failed unevaluated case.
findings.evidence: Direct rendering through CycleTally and cycle_view printed 'failed 2 Show 1 skipped record'. Tests cover Failed unevaluated-only and Partial malformed-plus-unevaluated cases, but omit their Failed mixed combination.
findings.suggested_fix: Require ns.unevaluated == 0 in the skipped-record branch so Failed mixed cycles reach the failure-reason fallback. Add a regression asserting 'Show 2 failure reasons' for this combination and absence of the skipped-record summary.

findings.title: Concurrent identical review runs can overwrite immutable evidence
findings.trigger: Two invocations use the same head, label, and attempt before either finishes pytest and creates its first output.
findings.execution_path: Both execute calls see no existing outputs, create independent temporary worktrees, and proceed. _run_pytest uses write_text, _run_codex opens the shared event file with mode 'w' and passes the same final-report destination to Codex, and both executions write the same status file.
findings.consequence: One invocation can overwrite another's original findings or leave a report, event stream, test evidence, and assessment from different invocations under one attempt identity, violating the immutable evidence contract.
findings.evidence: The existence check does not reserve the output identity. There is no lock or exclusive creation before the potentially 30-minute pytest operation. The overwrite regression only tests an output that exists before execute starts, so it does not protect this interleaving.
findings.suggested_fix: Atomically reserve the head/label/attempt identity before starting work, reject duplicate reservations, and retain the reservation through output publication. Add a concurrency regression proving the second invocation cannot launch or overwrite evidence.
findings.hypothesis: Two processes passing the initial existence check before the first output is created will subsequently write the same destinations. This interleaving was established by code inspection but not exercised with live concurrent Codex processes.
